subject: Platform Engage — RSVP wave & geo-snooze matrix
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Planning] RSVP wave plan + geo-snooze matrix for Platform Engage (Sept)

Hi team,

Per our prep for the Platform Engage inbound webinar (target date: Sept 15), I sketched an initial RSVP wave plan that prioritizes APAC/EU engineering windows and staggers reminders to reduce spam complaints. The attached heatmap shows expected open rates by timezone bucket and previous webinar engagement.

Asks:
- Marissa: can you review the 3 suggested reminder cadences (T-10 / T-3 / day-of) and confirm which we should A/B test for engineering vs product personas?
- Vivek: can you validate the proposed times for the live demo and the backup times for partner co-hosts?
- Kimberley: please confirm tracking link strategy (we should include a UTM per wave + unique RSVP token). I left a sample tracking_links_utm_v3.csv attached.

Notes:
- I propose a geo-snooze window: if an attendee clicks but doesn't RSVP, we wait 7 days before re-including in a subsequent nurture.
- For enterprise accounts (Acme Platform), we'll send a dedicated VIP wave with earlier reminders — looping in Samir below.

Attachments: rsvp_geo_heatmap_v1.xlsx, tracking_links_utm_v3.csv

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Growth Programs Manager | Events
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Planning] RSVP wave plan + geo-snooze matrix for Platform Engage (Sept)

Thanks Jonas — great start. Quick notes inline.

- Cadences: agree to test T-10 (intro), T-3 (technical teaser with workload examples), and a short day-of reminder for registrants who started but didn't complete RSVP. For engineers, swap the T-3 creative to include a short benchmark image.
- A/B: we should randomize send times within each timezone bucket (±60 min) to avoid throttling by recipient providers.
- VIP (Acme): recommend sending the VIP wave 48 hours earlier than the general wave; include co-host slot offer and 1:1 office hours link.

I updated tracking_links_utm_v3.csv with two additional params: utm_wave and rsvp_token. Uploaded to the shared sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Xq_wV-wave-cadence (see tab 'UTM by wave').

Small request: can Kimberly add per-wave reply-to override (events@ redwood) so RSVP confirmations go to the events alias? Also — flag for legal: are there any required consent/opt-out differences for Acme contacts?

On the heatmap: I see a dip for Mountain time around 11:00am — likely because of internal meeting windows. Suggest we avoid a hard send at 11:00 for that bucket.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference
